title: Digital misinformation and antimicrobial stewardship: cross-platform epidemiologic signals from a decade of online discourse (2015-2025)
screen_reason: Cross-platform infodemiology study of 1.8 million antibiotic-related posts from Twitter/X, Reddit and Facebook (2015-2025), classified by a transformer-based NLP pipeline. The abstract reports a single explicit share with a denominator: 'Misinformation comprised 19.3% of posts' - a CONTENT estimate. Abstract only; no methods or results section available.

estimates.country: Not stated (public data from Twitter/X, Reddit and Facebook; global WHO GLASS resistance measures used as the comparison series)
estimates.measure_type: % of antibiotic-related social media posts classified as misinformation
estimates.value_raw: Misinformation comprised 19.3% of posts (of 1.8 million posts containing antibiotic-related key terms)
estimates.denominator: 1.8 million public posts containing antibiotic-related key terms, extracted from Twitter/X, Reddit and Facebook, 2015-2025
estimates.definition: Post assigned to a misinformation class by transformer-based classification; four dominant misinformation themes reported: self-medication advocacy, natural-remedy promotion, allegations of hidden motives or suppressed evidence, and anti-medical discourse
estimates.misinfo_def: No explicit definition given in the abstract beyond the object of study, 'antibiotic-related misinformation', operationalised via the four themes: "self-medication advocacy, natural-remedy promotion, misinformation alleging hidden motives or suppressed evidence, and anti-medical discourse"
estimates.source_quote: Results: Misinformation comprised 19.3% of posts, spreading 2.4 times faster than factual content ( p <.001).
estimates.ground_truth_detail: "Natural-language processing and transformer-based classification identified misinformation themes, sentiment polarity, and diffusion dynamics." No training data, human-validation subsample, accuracy, F1 or inter-rater statistic is reported in the abstract, and no full text is available to check.
estimates.moderator_quote: Methods: We extracted 1.8 million posts containing antibiotic-related key terms. Natural-language processing and transformer-based classification identified misinformation themes, sentiment polarity, and diffusion dynamics.
estimates.notes: Abstract-only appraisal. confidence=low for three reasons: (a) the classifier is entirely unvalidated in the available text - no accuracy or human check is reported, and classifier-based prevalence is the least reliable ground truth in the schema; (b) the denominator is a rounded '1.8 million', so no exact part/whole check is possible; (c) the estimate is pooled over three platforms and a ten-year window, and no platform-specific or year-specific breakdown is given, so it cannot be disaggregated (and must not be split into invented sub-rows). breadth=misleading because the four themes (self-medication advocacy, natural-remedy promotion, suppressed-evidence claims, anti-medical discourse) are advocacy/insinuation categories rather than verifiably false factual claims. year=2025 is the end of the 2015-2025 collection decade; the midpoint would be ~2020 if the review prefers midpoints.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) 'spreading 2.4 times faster than factual content (p < .001)' is a diffusion-speed ratio, not a share of anything, so no row. (2) The four dominant misinformation themes are named but no per-theme share of posts is given, so they cannot become definition-variant rows. (3) The correlation with antibiotic search intent (rho = .74, p < .001) and the 6-9 month lead over resistance trends for E. coli, K. pneumoniae and S. aureus are associations, not prevalence. (4) No platform-specific breakdown of the 19.3% is reported even though three platforms were pooled, and no year-by-year series is given despite the decade-long window; splitting the pooled figure would violate the no-invented-sub-rows rule. (5) Network/echo-chamber analysis (Gephi) is mentioned but no top-X%/share-of-activity pair is reported, so no CONCENTRATION row is possible (R1). (6) Only the abstract was available; the full text would be needed to verify the classifier, the exact denominator, and whether platform-level shares exist.

rob.design: Retrospective cross-platform infodemiology study, 2015-2025, of 1.8 million public posts containing antibiotic-related key terms from Twitter/X, Reddit and Facebook, classified for misinformation by NLP and transformer-based models, with topic modelling and Gephi network analysis, and cross-correlation / Granger lead-lag tests against WHO GLASS antimicrobial-resistance indicators. Sampling frame is a keyword capture with no stated random or census basis; no response rate applies; no coding reliability, classifier accuracy, or human validation is reported anywhere in the available abstract; country coverage and language restrictions are unstated. Abstract-only appraisal - risk of bias cannot be judged beyond the fact that the central prevalence rests on an unvalidated automated classifier.
rob.item6_quote: Natural-language processing and transformer-based classification identified misinformation themes, sentiment polarity, and diffusion dynamics.
rob.item10_quote: We extracted 1.8 million posts containing antibiotic-related key terms. ... Misinformation comprised 19.3% of posts, spreading 2.4 times faster than factual content ( p <.001).
